SITUATION: A lone goblin skulker with a copper dagger is closing on the adventurer from 12 tiles on an open road; the adventurer is healthy with a steel short sword.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Goblin morale and breaking points | Goblins are small and break off when their leader dies or when they take a wound; a single skulker usually flees after the first solid hit.
[C2] Crossing rivers in adventure mode | Fords are safer than swimming; a rope helps on steep banks and armor should be removed before swimming.
[C3] Typical caravan prices | Food, rope and waterskins cost a few dozen coins at a dwarven caravan.
[C4] Brewing dwarven ale | Pig tails and cave wheat are brewed at a still and stored in barrels.

SITUATION: A bronze colossus is walking towards the unarmored adventurer across open ground 10 tiles away; the adventurer carries only a copper dagger.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Bronze colossus | A bronze colossus is a huge animated statue; ordinary weapons barely scratch it and it never flees, so fighting one on open ground is suicide.
[C2] Breaking line of sight | Most hostile creatures lose track of the adventurer when sight is broken behind terrain, and slow creatures give up sooner.
[C3] Tavern songs of the region | Innkeepers pay a few coins for a song or a story about local heroes.
[C4] Mushroom farming | Cave wheat and plump helmets grow on muddied floor tiles underground.

SITUATION: The adventurer is bleeding from a deep leg wound after a trap; no hostiles in sight; bandages and a waterskin are in the pack.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Bandaging wounds | A bandage applied to a bleeding wound stops the bleeding; an undressed wound keeps bleeding.
[C2] Pressure on a bleeding limb | Firm pressure on the wound slows blood loss while the bandage is prepared and while walking.
[C3] Smelting iron ore | Iron ore is smelted with coke or charcoal at a smelter to produce iron bars.
[C4] Goblin language phrases | A few goblin words let the adventurer understand war cries and insults.

SITUATION: The adventurer has not eaten for two days and is getting weak; no food in the pack; the road crosses a temperate forest with a campfire site.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Edible wild plants | In temperate biomes the adventurer can gather edible roots, berries and mushrooms; some mushrooms are poisonous.
[C2] Cooking at a campfire | Raw meat and fish must be cooked at a campfire before eating, and cooking removes some poisons.
[C3] Forging a steel short sword | Steel is made from iron and flux at a smelter and forged at a forge with fuel.
[C4] Dwarven noble succession | Fortress nobles are appointed by the monarch and pass the title to their heirs.

SITUATION: The road to the fortress is blocked by a rockfall and the adventurer must find another way through the hills before night.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Reading terrain for passable routes | Valleys, game trails and dry riverbeds lead through hills faster than climbing, and steep slopes cost stamina.
[C2] Regional road network | The old trade road runs east of the hills and rejoins the fortress road at the river.
[C3] Wrestling techniques | Wrestling lets the adventurer grab and throw a smaller opponent or break a hold.
[C4] Soap making | Soap is made from tallow and lye at a soap maker's shop.

SITUATION: A human hunter is skinning a deer in the clearing; the adventurer is healthy, lost and needs directions to the fortress.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Greetings that make NPCs friendly | A polite greeting and a small gift raise an NPC's disposition, while a hostile greeting starts a fight.
[C2] Asking NPCs for directions | Hunters and travelling merchants answer questions about roads and landmarks they have seen.
[C3] Sharpening a blade | A whetstone sharpens a blade and improves its cutting.
[C4] Cave geology strata | Limestone, chalk and dolomite layers are sedimentary and carry iron ore and gems.

SITUATION: A dwarven merchant caravan is stopped at the roadside; the adventurer has 300 coins and no food left.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Caravan food prices | Dried meat, fish and cheap drink cost a few coins each at a dwarven caravan, and waterskins cost more.
[C2] Bartering etiquette | Merchants improve a deal when the adventurer offers something they want and does not haggle too hard.
[C3] Rumours from merchants | Merchants trade news about closed roads, bandit camps and creature sightings on their route.
[C4] Crossbow maintenance | A crossbow's string is waxed and replaced when it frays, and bolts are stored dry.

SITUATION: It is night in a wolf-filled forest, howls are close, and the exhausted adventurer must decide where to spend the night.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Choosing a camp site | A camp behind a narrow entrance or on high ground is much harder for animals to reach, while open ground invites attacks.
[C2] Sleep and watch rotation | An exhausted adventurer sleeps deeply and can be surprised; a companion on watch wakes them in time.
[C3] Engraving stone | Engravers decorate walls and floors with images of the fortress's history.

SITUATION: Noon on a known, safe trade road; the adventurer is healthy, fed, watered and rested, one day from the fortress, with nothing to decide beyond walking on.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Legendary swords of the age | Named artefacts have their own histories and some are said to cut through bronze.
[C2] Dwarven mining songs | Miners sing while they work; the songs name the mountain and the ancestors.
[C3] Cheese aging | Cheese is aged in a food stockpile and improves in value with time.
[C4] History of a distant fortress | A fortress three regions away was founded two centuries ago and abandoned after a siege.

SITUATION: The adventurer is standing at a friendly caravan with 300 coins, a full waterskin and no wounds; nothing threatens and no decision is pending.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Slaying a dragon | Dragons breathe fire and shrug off ordinary steel; they must be fought with ranged weapons from cover.
[C2] Siege engineering | Catapults and ballistae are built at a siege workshop and need operators.
[C3] Ancient curses of the region | Old curses are recorded in slabs and some are said to follow grave robbers.

SITUATION: The adventurer stands at the mouth of an unknown cave that may lead to the objective; it is dark inside and the tunnels are unmapped.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Light in the dark | Adventure mode needs a light source underground, and torches burn down and can be refilled.
[C2] How caves branch | Caves follow water and ore veins; junctions usually mean one branch descends and one dead-ends.
[C3] Farming seasons above ground | Crops are planted in spring and harvested in autumn on the surface.
[C4] Fishing with a net | A net catches several fish at once in shallow water.

SITUATION: After looting a bandit camp the adventurer is overloaded, moving slowly, with a hostile camp 20 tiles away.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] How weight slows the adventurer | Above the carry limit the adventurer moves slower and tires faster, and speed drops with every extra item.
[C2] What to drop first | Drop bulky low-value items first and keep food, water, weapons and bandages.
[C3] Goblin war cries | Goblin war cries signal an attack and roughly how many are coming.

SITUATION: The adventurer must cross a wide river at a ford before dark; the current looks strong and the pack is heavy.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Armor and swimming | Heavy armor and a heavy pack make swimming dangerous, and removing them before entering deep water is safer.
[C2] Fighting underwater | Weapons swing slowly underwater and grappling works better; most creatures cannot drown the adventurer.
[C3] Rope making | Rope is made from plant fibre at a rope maker's shop.
